patients.summary: Retired math teacher with hypertension, BPH and diverticulosis who joined in 2024. Adhesive small-bowel obstruction needed laparotomy, complicated by a catheter-related bulbar urethral injury; chronic retention led to a bladder stone, and two weeks after its removal he developed enterococcal tricuspid endocarditis treated with six weeks of ampicillin and ceftriaxone.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

66 y/o man, retired after 31 years teaching math (mostly algebra II and calc), here to establish. Previous PCP was fine, he just wants someone closer who answers the phone.

Current issues: none acute. Feels well.

HTN - diagnosed in his 50s, has been on amlodipine plus lisinopril for years. Doesn't check at home regularly, has an old cuff. No headaches, CP, SOB, swelling.
BPH - urology dx several years back. On tamsulosin, gets up once at night, stream 'slower than it used to be but fine.' No retention episodes, no UTIs. Hasn't seen urology in a couple years.
Diverticulosis - found on his colonoscopy in 2019, never had diverticulitis. Mother had diverticular trouble too.

PSH: gallbladder out through an open incision, long ago, can't remember the year. Nothing else.
Meds: amlodipine 5 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, tamsulosin 0.4 daily. No OTCs.
Allergies: none to meds.
FH: father had high BP and coronary disease. Mother diverticular disease.
SH: smoked about 15 pack-years, quit ~12 yrs ago. Wine or a beer once or twice a month. No drugs ever. Walks most mornings. Retired from teaching high school math.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pleasant, well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no bruits, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, well-healed right subcostal scar. No edema, pulses 2+ distally. Skin fine.

A/P
1. HTN - reasonable on current regimen, continue amlodipine 5 + lisinopril 10. CMP today.
2. BPH with LUTS - stable on tamsulosin, continue. Will need urology again if anything changes.
3. Diverticulosis - fiber, fluids. Colonoscopy records requested.
4. Former smoker - 15 pk-yr so below the threshold for lung screening.
5. HM - high-dose flu and PCV20 today. Hep C and HIV screens with labs. Lipids. PHQ-2 0.

RTC 3-4 months for BP, sooner prn. Texting line explained.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Walter - labs from Tuesday all look good. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the lisinopril, blood counts normal, liver tests normal. Cholesterol numbers are fine. Hep C and HIV screens negative, so those are done for good. Nothing to change. Talk soon.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Quicker than I'm used to.

events.reason: abdominal pain, vomiting, no stool or gas

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
INDICATION: Small-bowel obstruction on radiograph, prior open cholecystectomy.
TECHNIQUE: Axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast, with coronal and sagittal reformats. Oral contrast not given.
FINDINGS: Multiple fluid-filled dilated small-bowel loops measuring up to 3.6 cm, with a transition point in the mid abdomen and collapsed distal ileum. No discrete mass at the transition. No closed-loop configuration. Bowel wall enhances normally; no pneumatosis, portal venous gas or free air. Small amount of free fluid between loops. Colon decompressed; scattered sigmoid diverticula without inflammation. Surgically absent gallbladder. Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. Abdominal aorta normal in caliber. Bladder partially distended. Prostate mildly enlarged. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Small-bowel obstruction with a mid-abdominal transition point, likely adhesive. No closed loop or signs of ischemia. Sigmoid diverticulosis.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 11/28/2024

CC: belly pain and vomiting

HPI: 67M with HTN, BPH and diverticulosis, remote open cholecystectomy, here with two days of crampy, severe generalized abdominal pain coming in waves, several episodes of emesis, and no bowel movement or flatus since the day before yesterday. Denies fevers or chills. No blood in emesis.

Meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. NKDA.
FH: father HTN and CAD; mother diverticular disease.
SH: ex-smoker (15 pk-yr, quit 12 yr ago), rare alcohol, retired math teacher.

Triage: BP 150/90, HR 110, RR 22, T 37.2 C.

Exam: uncomfortable, retching. Abdomen visibly distended and tympanitic, tender throughout but no rebound and no guarding. Tinkling, high-pitched, hyperactive bowel sounds. Old RUQ incision. DRE: vault empty, no mass.

Labs: WBC 14.0 K. Rest of CBC and BMP unremarkable.
Upright abdominal film: dilated small-bowel loops with numerous air-fluid levels, no gas in the rectum.
CT A/P w contrast: SBO with mid-abdominal transition, no closed loop or ischemic signs, presumed adhesive.

Course: IV fluids, ondansetron, IV analgesia. NG tube placed with large bilious return and relief. General surgery consulted, recommends admission for nonoperative trial.

Dx: small-bowel obstruction, likely adhesive.
Dispo: admit to general surgery.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: General Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admission 11/28/2024 - Discharge 12/02/2024
Service: General Surgery

Admitting dx: adhesive small-bowel obstruction
Discharge dx: same, resolved without operation

Hospital course: Admitted from ED with SBO on CT, mid-abdominal transition point, no ischemic features. Managed with NG decompression, bowel rest, IV fluids and serial abdominal exams. NG output fell steadily, he passed flatus on hospital day 2 and had a BM on day 3. NG removed 12/1, clears advanced to regular diet and tolerated. Abdomen soft and nondistended at discharge. Home antihypertensives held while NPO and resumed 12/1.

Discharge meds: unchanged - amlodipine 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA

Instructions: soft diet for a few days then advance. Return for recurrent pain, vomiting, distension or no flatus. Discussed that adhesions can cause this again and may need surgery if so.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks. Surgery clinic as needed.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after receiving hospital paperwork. Home since Monday. Eating soups and toast, had a normal BM yesterday, passing gas. No vomiting, mild soreness only. Taking his 3 usual meds. Knows to call or go back in if the pain or vomiting returns. Booked with PCP 12/9.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after admission 11/28-12/2 for adhesive SBO, settled with NG tube and bowel rest, no surgery. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed; CT showed mid-abdominal transition, no ischemia.

Since home: back to regular food, BMs daily, no cramping or bloating. Lost a couple of pounds while in. Energy coming back.

Meds reconciled, unchanged: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Abdomen soft, not distended, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Old subcostal scar.

A/P
Adhesive SBO, resolved nonoperatively - likely from the old open gallbladder surgery. Reviewed warning signs; low threshold to go in if it recurs. Small, frequent meals for a bit.
HTN - fine today, no change.
Follow up in March for BP, sooner prn.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, max 6 tablets per day

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Date of operation: 12/31/2024
Preop dx: recurrent adhesive small-bowel obstruction
Postop dx: same
Procedure: exploratory laparotomy, lysis of adhesions
Anesthesia: general endotracheal

Findings: dense band adhesions from the old right upper quadrant field to mid small bowel producing an obstruction, dilated proximal loops, decompressed distal ileum. All bowel viable after release; no resection required. No hernia, no mass.

Description: Midline laparotomy. Adhesiolysis performed sharply, small bowel run from ligament to ileocecal valve twice, no enterotomy. Abdomen irrigated, fascia closed with running looped suture, skin with staples. Urethral catheter placed at start of case. EBL 50 mL. To PACU stable.
